provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The emitted program does not use any normalisation step. Rotation by 90 or 270 degrees (odd d4) turns the horizontal band of full-width rows into a vertical band of full-height columns. So the factory sets AXIS=1 for odd d4, and the program then reads, stamps and tiles columns directly. For even d4 it works on rows. A reflection or 180-degree rotation keeps the band on the same axis. Because the tiling covers both directions symmetrically and is anchored at the band itself, no direction constant needs reversing. The background is the constant palette[0]. Algorithm: (1) find the contiguous span of lines along the active axis that contain any non-background cell; this span is the band, with start y0 and height h. (2) Copy the band's lines. (3) Stamp copies at y0 - k*p going backward and y0 + k*p going forward, clipped at the grid edges. Only non-background cells are written, which matches the generator's draw-overlay semantics. When p = h, every line is fully determined as band[(y - y0) mod h]. The period p defaults to the band height, which is the stated rule. As a safeguard, the program first checks whether the demonstrations agree with p = h. If they do not, it searches for a single constant period that reproduces every demonstration output and uses that instead.
draft_notes.limitations: Constructor issue for host review: the generator always tiles with a fixed vertical step of 3 (range(-6, height, 3)), not with the band height. It draws only coloured pixels, so copies are overlaid rather than replacing whole rows. This matches the stated rule only when the sprite really spans 3 rows. With flip=1, the union across tiles always spans 3 rows. With flip=0, conway_sprite(randint(2,3), 3) could in principle produce a sprite occupying fewer than 3 rows. The output would then have period 3 with blank lines while the band height is smaller, which contradicts the rule as written. The emitted solver follows the stated band-height rule. It falls back to a demo-inferred constant period only when the demos contradict that rule. If a query's band height differs from what the demos imply in such a degenerate case, the result follows the demo-consistent period. The background is assumed to be palette[0], as in every generator output. Grids with no non-background cells are returned unchanged. None of this has been run or tested.
draft_notes.host_review: Inspected common.py: conway_sprite preserves at least one pixel in every row and column; independent row/column shuffles preserve this property, so its full bounding box is visible. random_color/random_colors exclude background 0. overlaps with spacing=1 requires a full-cell gap. Domain concerns contingent on these helpers are resolved.
